newsitem.title: USA: Florida home resales drop 7 pct from April 1996.
newsitem.headline: Florida home resales drop 7 pct from April 1996.

text.p: Florida sales of existing single-family homes totalled 11,253 in April, an increase of 4 percent over March but down 7 percent from April of last year, the Florida Association of Realtors said Tuesday.
The median sales price was $92,300, unchanged from March but up 3 percent from April 1996.

A slight rise in interest rates contributed to slower home resales in some areas, as did larger inventories of new homes and the residual effects of sizzling sales in early 1996, the association said.
In April 1996, when the average interest rate for a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage was 7.93 percent, home resales jumped 25 percent above the prior-year level.
Realtors said last year's buying rush satisfied much of the pent-up demand for first-time and move-up homes. In April 1997, the average rate for a comparable mortgage was 8.14 percent.
The metropolitan Jacksonville area saw home resales rise by 4 percent over last April, fueled by corporate expansion and recruitment of out-of-state companies.
In the Fort Myers-Cape Coral area, resales jumped 45 percent as the region prepared for the fall opening of Florida's tenth university, Florida Gulfcoast University.
Home resales in the Panama City area rose 26 percent, to 159 sales, while the median price fell 8 percent to $73,000.
"In general terms, when interest rates rise you find that lower-priced homes sell," said Joe W. Jegg, office manager for St. Andrew Bay Real Estate's Tyndall Parkway office.

The Melbourne-Titusville area posted a 10 percent increase over April a year ago, a gain attributed to aggressive economic development, renewed port activity and increased hiring by small and large companies.
Other Florida metropolitan areas and their changes over year-ago levels were:

Fort Lauderdale, down 27 percent; Tallahassee and West Palm Beach, both down 25 percent; Pensacola, down 23 percent; Gainesville, down 14 percent; Fort Walton Beach, down 11 percent; Orlando and Punta Gorda, both down 10 percent; Miami, down 9 percent; Port St. Lucie and Naples , both down 2 percent; and Tampa-St. Petersburg, down one percent
Sarasota-Bradenton, up 9 percent; Ocala, up 5 percent; and Lakeland-Winter Haven, up 2 percent.
Daytona Beach was unchanged from April of last year.
